title: Linking and asking: és, de, mert, hanem, is

sections.content: Small joining words make longer sentences. *És* adds an idea and *de* sets one against another, with a comma before *de*: *A szoba kicsi, de világos.* *Mert* starts a reason with its own verb, with a comma before it: *Nem főzök, mert olvasok.* To correct a mistake, put *nem* before the wrong word and *hanem* before the right one: *Nem Anna főz, hanem Károly.* *Is* goes right after the word it adds to: *Meg is dolgozik.*

items.english: The flat is small, but comfortable.
I do not cook, because I read.

items.spanish: Nem a boltba megyek, hanem a parkba.
items.english: I am not going to the shop but to the park.

sections.content: *Miért* asks and *mert* answers. *Hanem* needs a *nem* before it. For a plain reason use *mert* with a whole clause that has its own verb.
